title: FAA UAP reports, batch 04 (237UAP00082 - 237UAP00106)
doc_notes: This document is a collection of FAA Skywatch incident reports regarding UAP sightings by commercial and general aviation pilots between March and August 2022.

incidents.summary: Aircraft observed a line of stationary strobe lights far above their altitude.
incidents.quote: observing a possible UFO with a line of stationary strobe lights far above his aircraft

incidents.summary: Unidentified aircraft broadcasted presence of UAP; pilot reported rapid vertical and lateral movement.
incidents.quote: The unknown phenomenon was rapidly moving vertically and laterally up to 8,000 feet.

incidents.summary: Two aircraft reported an object resembling a rocket with a flash.
incidents.quote: reported an unidentified aerial phenomenon that appeared to be rocket with a flash traveling NW.

incidents.summary: Two aircraft reported an unidentified phenomenon; authorities concluded it was likely space debris.
incidents.quote: concluded that the unknown phenomenon given the pilots description was probably space debris.

incidents.summary: Pilot reported lights orbiting at high altitude; radar showed no activity.
incidents.quote: reporting observing 60-80 miles ahead and altitude very high above them several lights doing an orbit.

incidents.summary: Two aircraft reported lights maneuvering at high altitude.
incidents.quote: observing a set of lights very high in the distance maneuvering

incidents.summary: String of lights observed; aircraft experienced multiple system failures while underneath.
incidents.quote: LXJ359 experienced a double Attitude Reference System failure and a double Autopilot System failure while directly underneath of the UFO lights.

incidents.summary: Lights observed maneuvering between FL300 and FL400.
incidents.quote: The unknown phenomenon was lights maneuvering between approximately FL300 and FL400.

incidents.summary: Two aircraft reported an equally spaced line of bright lights moving eastward.
incidents.quote: an equally spaced line of very bright lights moving Eastward away from their aircraft

incidents.summary: Object observed traveling at altitude; no traffic on radar or TCAS.
incidents.quote: The unknown phenomenon was described as an object traveling E to W bound at approximately same altitude.

incidents.summary: Lights observed at high altitude with no contrail.
incidents.quote: The unknown phenomenon was described as lights with no contrail traveling at approximately FL 600 or above.

incidents.summary: Stationary, untethered object observed passing underneath aircraft.
incidents.quote: The unknown phenomenon was stationary and untethered with no lights.

incidents.summary: Three lights observed turning on and off, stationary above the horizon.
incidents.quote: The unknown phenomenon was 3 lights turning on and off, above the horizon stationary.

incidents.summary: Two to three stationary lights appearing and disappearing.
incidents.quote: The unknown phenomenon was 2 to 3 stationary lights appearing and disappearing.

incidents.summary: Flashing lights observed in a diamond pattern traveling west to east.
incidents.quote: The unknown phenomenon was described as flashing lights traveling west to east in a diamond pattern

incidents.summary: Lights observed making 360-degree turns; possibly Starlink satellites.
incidents.quote: observed the lights and believes they are Starlink satellites.

incidents.summary: Lights observed in racetrack pattern; possibly Starlink satellites.
incidents.location_name: 1,050 miles off the E coast of the Carolinas
incidents.quote: They report this sighting to possibly be Starlink Satellites.

incidents.summary: Green light observed traveling at low altitude.
incidents.quote: The unknown phenomenon was a green light traveling W bound at approximately 50 feet.

incidents.summary: Three lights in a row observed in geosynchronous orbit.
incidents.quote: The unknown phenomenon was described as 3 lights in a row and above them in a geosynchronous orbit.

incidents.summary: Bright light observed in a holding pattern; possibly Starlink satellites.
incidents.quote: PIC indicated they though phenomenon was star link satellites reflecting sunlight.

incidents.summary: Bright light observed in a holding pattern.
incidents.quote: The unknown phenomenon was a bright light in a holding pattern approximately 5,000 feet above.
